name: Sea Island Creole English

ancestors.notes: Descent per Glottolog classification of Sea Island Creole English (gull1241).
English superstrate/lexifier of Gullah, from the English of Sea Island coastal-Carolina/Georgia planters and traders (Turner 1949).

Kikongo (Kongo) substrate, one of the West African source languages named by APiCS (survey ch. 13, apics-online.info/surveys/13: 'Fula, Kongo, Mende, Vai, Yoruba') as figuring prominently in the texts, personal names and words Turner (1949) collected; no source ranks it as the largest single contributor.

Fula (Fulani) substrate, named in APiCS survey ch. 13 (apics-online.info/surveys/13); Wikipedia additionally records Gullah speakers who could recite songs and do simple counting in Fulani alongside Mende and Vai (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gullah_language).
Yoruba substrate, named in APiCS survey ch. 13 (apics-online.info/surveys/13) among the West African languages prominent in Turner's (1949) Gullah word/name corpus.

notes: Skeleton. English-lexifier creole of the South Carolina and Georgia Sea Islands, written in a Latin, largely English-based spelling. Grapheme map uses English digraph conventions (ch, sh, ng; oo [u], ee [i]) but reflects the creole's own phonology where it diverges, notably th realised as a stop [t]/[d]. Gullah has no fixed standard orthography and much text is eye-dialect respelling of English; unstressed-vowel reduction and any prosodic detail are not recoverable and are left unencoded, so a real PER floor is expected.
